target.title: fix(subagents): killed subagent runs stay running in the task list
target.body:
**Prompt request:** Make every path that kills a subagent run finalize its detached task-registry row, so the task list reflects the kill instead of showing the task as running forever, while leaving the kill and abort behavior itself unchanged.

**Proof target:** Show that after a `subagents` kill the killed run's task row flips to `cancelled`, while normal completion and failure transitions go through unchanged code paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who kill a running subagent (via the `subagents` kill tool, its kill-all and cascade variants, or by aborting the parent reply) keep seeing that task as `running` in `openclaw tasks list` indefinitely. The in-memory subagent registry records the kill and the chat reply says the run was killed, but the detached task-registry row is never finalized, so task surfaces disagree with what actually happened and the phantom `running` entry never clears.

## Why This Change Was Made

`markSubagentRunTerminated` sets `endedAt` synchronously, which short-circuits the completion watcher — the lifecycle finalizer that normally updates the task row never runs for killed runs, and no kill caller finalized the ledger itself. This change finalizes the task row as `cancelled` inside `markSubagentRunTerminated`, the termination primitive all kill paths funnel through (tool kill and its kill-all and cascade variants, admin kill, and the parent-reply abort path in `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts`). Already-ended entries are skipped so the finalize stays single-shot, and a finalize failure degrades to a warning without breaking termination. The operator `tasks cancel` path keeps its own status update, which now becomes an idempotent overwrite of the same state. If a kill races a completion that still lands, the row stays `cancelled` — the same sticky-cancelled outcome the operator `tasks cancel` path already produces in that race, since run-scoped updates never overwrite a cancelled row.

## User Impact

`openclaw tasks list` and task status surfaces now show killed subagent runs as `cancelled` (with a short reason) instead of a permanently `running` phantom entry. Successful, failed, and timed-out runs keep their existing transitions — those code paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture driving the production path with no mocks at any layer — real `registerSubagentRun`, real `subagents` kill, and `listTaskRecords` reading real registry rows from an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (a hanging gateway socket keeps the completion watcher pending, as it is while a real child run executes):

Before (main):

```
[after-spawn] taskId=65238e57-8192-4f19-bb8a-76ecf8c3d4ff runtime=subagent status=running error=-
[kill] status=ok text=killed proof task: long-running background work.
[after-kill] taskId=65238e57-8192-4f19-bb8a-76ecf8c3d4ff runtime=subagent status=running error=-
```

After (this PR):

```
[after-spawn] taskId=a06f3326-23f8-4900-a0a8-73251b0234ca runtime=subagent status=running error=-
[kill] status=ok text=killed proof task: long-running background work.
[after-kill] taskId=a06f3326-23f8-4900-a0a8-73251b0234ca runtime=subagent status=cancelled error=Subagent run killed.
```

Focused tests: `src/agents/subagent-control.test.ts` (30 passed) — a tool kill finalizes the row as `cancelled`, a rejected kill leaves the ledger untouched, a throwing finalize still reports the kill, and the admin kill path finalizes the same way; the two ledger assertions fail without the fix. The kill-all and cascade variants are covered through the shared primitive. `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.test.ts` (31 passed) covers the parent-reply abort caller reaching the same termination primitive.
